---
title: "Demonstrating saving images from matrices"
format: pdf
---

```{r}
save_img <- function(x, file) {
  # x: matrix of pixel values (0-1)
  # file: path to save the image (e.g., "reconstructed_image.jpg").
  #       Must specify file extension as .jpg, .png or .pdf.
  if (grepl("\\.jpg$", file)) {
    save_func <- jpeg::writeJPEG
  } else if (grepl("\\.png$", file)) {
    save_func <- png::writePNG
  } else if (grepl("\\.pdf$", file)) {
      save_func <- function(x, file) {
        pdf(file, width = ncol(x)/100, height = nrow(x)/100)
        par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
        plot(NA, NA, xlim = c(0, ncol(x)), ylim = c(0, nrow(x)), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
        rasterImage(x, 0, 0, ncol(x), nrow(x))
        dev.off()
      }
  } else {
    stop("Unsupported file format. Use .jpg or .png")
  }
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(x))) {
    x[, j] <- pmax(pmin(1, x[, j]), 0)
  }
  save_func(
    x,
    file
  )
  file
}
```

```{r}
# "data" specifying image,
# where each element is the darkness of a pixel
# with 0 being black and 1 being white.
# here I made up a matrix, where the first
# n_row rows are just black,
# the next n_row rows are all white,
# the next n_row rows range from black to white,
# and the final n_row rows are random
n_col <- 2000
n_row <- 150
img_mat <- rbind(
  lapply(seq_len(n_row), function(x) rep(0,n_col)) |> unlist() |> matrix(ncol = n_col),
  lapply(seq_len(n_row), function(x) rep(1,n_col)) |> unlist() |> matrix(ncol = n_col),
  lapply(seq_len(n_row), function(x) seq(0, 1, length.out = n_col)) |> unlist() |> matrix(ncol = n_col, byrow = TRUE),
  lapply(seq_len(n_row), function(x) runif(n_col)) |> unlist() |> matrix(ncol = n_col, byrow = TRUE)
)
```

```{r}
# where you want to save the image
# (include image extension, e.g. png or jpg or pdf).
# when you're rending to pdf, make the extension pdf,
# but when you're rendering to html, use png or jpg
path_img <- "photo_of_the_year.pdf"
# save the image, where the first argument
# is the matrix of pixel darkness values
# and the second argument is the path
# to save the image to
save_img(img_mat, path_img)
```

```{r, results="asis"}
# display the image, which has been saved 
# to file, in the rendered document
knitr::include_graphics(path_img)
```

The whole goal in the PCA question is to come up with the appropriate matrices to pass to `save_img`.
